effects: The signer's LLCassaUSDC vault shares (amount = shares) are pulled from the signer into the withdrawal queue, using the signer's allowance on the vault token.
A withdrawal-request NFT is minted to `receiver`. It is the only right to claim the underlying assets later, so if `receiver` is not the signer, the signer gives that right away.
How many underlying assets the request pays out is decided later, when the queue is filled at the vault's redeem rate. Nothing about it is fixed now.
The queue then calls sweepPending() on the vault's delegator. This is protocol housekeeping and moves none of the signer's assets.
formats.shown: Request queued withdrawal: queue N LLCassaUSDC shares of vault 0xCed0…, with the withdrawal NFT sent to the receiver.

findings.title: requestRedeem: 'NFT recipient' does not say the NFT is the only right to claim the withdrawn assets.
findings.evidence: WithdrawalQueue.sol requestRedeem: `_mint(receiver, tokenId);` and claim: `if (ownerOf(tokenId) != msg.sender) revert NotTokenOwner();`. Descriptor field `#.receiver` label 'NFT recipient', interpolatedIntent 'Queue {shares}, NFT to {receiver}'.
findings.fix: Label the field 'Withdrawal claim (NFT) owner' and use an interpolatedIntent such as 'Queue {shares} for withdrawal; claim rights go to {receiver}'.

findings.title: requestRedeem: the asset amount paid out later is set at fill time and cannot be shown now.
findings.evidence: WithdrawalQueue.sol fill(): `assets = IERC4626(vault).redeem(shares, address(this), address(this));` stores cumulative assets per filled share, and claimable() uses those checkpoints. The calldata carries only the share count.
findings.fix: Optionally say in the intent that the asset amount is set when the queue is filled.

effects: The signer must own withdrawal NFT `tokenId`. The NFT is not burned and stays with the signer.

The claimable part of the request is paid to `receiver` in the vault's underlying asset (vault.asset()). The amount comes from storage: fill checkpoints minus what was already claimed. It may be a partial amount, or zero if nothing has been filled yet.
The request's sharesClaimed goes up by the shares paid out, which reduces what the NFT can still claim.
formats.shown: Claim filled withdrawal #tokenId of vault 0xCed0… to the asset recipient.

findings.title: claim: the payout amount and asset come from storage and the vault, not from calldata.
findings.evidence: WithdrawalQueue.sol claim(): `(assets, shares) = claimable(tokenId); ... IERC20(IERC4626(vault).asset()).safeTransfer(receiver, assets);`. The descriptor's fields are only Vault, 'Withdrawal NFT ID' (raw) and 'Asset recipient'.
findings.fix: Optionally name the underlying asset in the intent (e.g. 'Claim USDC from filled withdrawal'), since the descriptor covers a single vault.

findings.title: claim: it can pay only the filled part, or zero, and the NFT keeps the remainder; the intent does not say so.
findings.evidence: WithdrawalQueue.sol claimable(): `endShares = Math.min(request.prevRequestSum + request.shares, totalFilled());` and claim() neither reverts on zero nor burns the NFT. Intent 'Claim filled withdrawal'.
findings.fix: Optionally reword to 'Claim the filled part of withdrawal {tokenId} to {receiver}'.

couldNotCheck: The vault/share token VaultV2 at 0xCed027AdBF0966447b25E16f943A10780D5D1c08 has no source in the directory. requestRedeem pulls the signer's shares through its transferFrom, and claim pays out the token returned by its asset(), so neither transfer could be confirmed from code.
The UniversalDelegator (VaultV2(vault).delegator()) has no source in the directory. requestRedeem calls its sweepPending() inside the signer's transaction.
